Beebeeb macOS Popover
Task 1683 · design for review · 30 Sep 2026

The macOS app becomes a menu-bar popover

A small panel that opens under the b icon, modelled on the Proton Drive popover you pointed to. The big settings window shrinks to four tabs and only opens when you ask for it.

“I want it more like how proton looks. Now also our version is not nicely aligned, not small, has too much info etc. Also when i just start beebeeb that window is randomly in the screen and not at the top bar. Often see too many windows going around.”Guus, 30 Sep 2026

The popover, state by state

Fixed at 372×488 pt, so it never jumps when the state changes. Header: account and storage. Body: activity or one message. Footer: the same three actions every time.

Amended 6 Oct 2026 (ruling R5, docs/specs/2026-10-06-macos-finder-setup-reconciler.md): the “Finder not added” state and its “Add to Finder” button are gone. Beebeeb adds itself after sign-in. “Finder add failed” shows one sentence and one action per reason.

Gear menu, Settings, placement

Settings keeps what a person actually changes. Raw paths, session details and “not wired up” text are gone.

Fewer windows

Counted from the desktop source at 0.8.6. Three Windows-only windows were being created, hidden, on macOS too. Conflicts each opened their own window automatically.

Why screenshot 3 broke

  • The whole page scrolled instead of the content pane, so the sidebar scrolled away and left an empty column. Reproduced: the page was 1125 px tall in a 540 px window.
  • A long file path could not wrap, so the content grew wider than its column and slid under the sidebar (“ync health”). Reproduced: 485 px of content in a 452 px pane.
  • The duplicate Finder error came from the same failure being saved (drawn as a banner) and returned (drawn as a toast). The toast title measured 1.1:1 contrast; the new colours measure 13.3:1.

Seven choices for you

Each has a recommendation. A one-word answer per number is enough, for example “1 ok, 3 translucent, 5 pause”.

  1. 1

    At login

    RecommendedShow nothing at login. Open the popover once, under the icon, after the first install only (not after updates).

    Today a window opens on every login.

  2. 2

    Dock icon

    RecommendedNo Dock icon normally; show one only while Settings, onboarding or a review window is open.

    Alternative: never show a Dock icon, even for Settings.

  3. 3

    Translucent popover?

    RecommendedOpaque (as drawn). It uses public macOS APIs only.

    Proton-style translucency needs a private-API flag that blocks a future Mac App Store release.

  4. 4

    Quick Search

    RecommendedCut from the main surface. Version history stays, in a single review window.

    Say if you want Quick Search kept.

  5. 5

    Third footer action

    RecommendedAdd storage, as Proton does.

    If an always-visible upsell feels wrong for our tone, Pause/Resume takes the slot.

  6. 6

    Where Settings and onboarding open

    RecommendedSettings opens top-right under the menu bar on the icon’s display. Onboarding stays centred (860×640 does not fit under an icon).

    Or anchor both near the icon.

  7. 7

    Errors: toast or inline

    RecommendedKeep the current rule (a transient action failure is a toast, a blocking failure is inline) and fix only the double render.

    Or: never toast an action failure.

What is not checked yet

  • These are browser renders on Linux. The menu bar and window chrome are drawn approximations of macOS, and nothing has run on a Mac yet.
  • The email, files and storage figures are invented examples.
  • Implementation starts after you approve, in nine slices. Each ships with tests that are seen failing first. The last rung is you on the next macOS alpha.
